text:
sarah: heads up — spotted something odd in audit logs, role_change events missing for a few service-account operations :thinking_face:

sarah: looked at /api/v1/service-accounts/assign-role requests from last 24h, several successful responses but no corresponding audit entry. filing here before I dig deeper.

devraj: can you paste the exact request you used?

sarah: sure — repro curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/api/v1/service-accounts/assign-role \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"service_account_id":"svc-123","role":"org_admin"}'
```

morgan: :eyes: which token scope was that? user token or service token?

sarah: service token from our infra automation (svc-deploy). token has scope:service_accounts:write. not an admin user token.

devraj: i'm trying this on staging — quick check: the code path for assign-role goes through graphQL mutation assignRole(serviceAccountId, role). there should be an audit.logEvent call in authorizeAndLog(). if that was skipped it means authorizeAndLog didn't run.

leo: I grep'd the repo — there's a short-circuit added in 2025-11 that bypasses middleware when an X-Internal header is present:
```
// in gateway middleware
if (req.headers['x-internal'] === 'true') return next('skip-auth-middleware');
```
looks like the infra automation sets X-Internal to true.

emily: oh no. so an internal header used for health checks is allowing role assignment without audit. sev?

sarah: i'm leaning P1 for now — potential privilege escalation + missing audit.

oncall-bot: @devraj @morgan @leo paging oncall:security - incident created (INC-2026-118). Severity: P1.

devraj: containment plan: 1) block endpoint for requests with X-Internal header, 2) rotate service tokens used by infra automation, 3) add temporary WAF rule to deny POST /api/v1/service-accounts/assign-role from internal CIDR if header present.

ryan: do we need to notify any customers? potentially only internal service identities affected. i'll prepare a short customer-facing comms draft if we find any customer-facing keys used.

morgan: i'm going to push a hotfix to reject X-Internal on any mutating endpoint. quick patch diff:
```diff
- if (req.headers['x-internal'] === 'true') return next('skip-auth-middleware');
+ if (req.headers['x-internal'] === 'true') {
+   // never bypass auth for state-changing endpoints
+   if (req.method !== 'GET') return res.status(403).send('forbidden');
+ }
```

leo: staging repro shows audit now logs the event after patch.

infra-bot: firewall rule applied: block POST /api/v1/service-accounts/assign-role from 10.0.0.0/8 with header x-internal. (rule id fw-8732)

emily: we should treat this as potential exposure of KMS-wrapped credentials. ask KMS team to produce key usage logs for any keys used by svc-deploy tokens in last 48h.

sarah: filed KMS request KR-452. asked for parity: list of decrypt operations and key IDs.

devraj: rotation note — rotating the service-account tokens will require re-deploying infra automation. scheduling with infra oncall.

ryan: product note — we need to confirm if any org_admin grants were applied to customer-visible accounts. if yes, escalate to legal/compliance.

emily: quick list of action items for post-incident: ["audit middleware test coverage", "ban x-internal bypass for mutating routes", "add CI check for header bypass usage", "rotate affected tokens & keys if usage found", "postmortem + timeline + comms"].

morgan: pushed hotfix to canary and rolled to 3 pods. monitoring shows assign-role returns 403 when x-internal set.

leo: adding an integration test: will call assignRole via a mock with x-internal and assert 403 and assert audit entry exists for allowed calls.

infra-bot: svc-deploy tokens rotated: svc-deploy-main, svc-deploy-backup. rotation performed by infra-team.

devraj: created PR to remove skip-auth-middleware code path entirely and replace with explicit allowlist for internal endpoints that are read-only. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/4821

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-118 status updated: contained -> mitigated.

emily: please attach any relevant logs to the incident ticket. I'll schedule a postmortem for tomorrow EOD.

sarah: short timeline for the postmortem: root cause = legacy header bypass introduced in 2025-11 + automation relied on it; remediation = hotfix + rotate tokens + firewall; follow-ups = audit tests, CI guard, KMS log review, customer impact check.

ryan: thanks all. I'll draft the internal comms and loop legal if KMS logs show customer keys involved.

morgan: one more thing — can we add an audit log retention and alert rule for role_change events with missing log entries? basically a reconciliation job: compare DB role assignments vs audit log entries and alert if mismatch > 0.

emily: good idea. that becomes a 2-week action item. adding to postmortem.

leo: closing notes: no evidence of abuse so far, but rotating tokens + KMS review is complete. will update ticket with KMS response when it arrives. :lock: :white_check_mark:
